page: OVHcloud d2-4 is a Discovery family virtual server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel processor based on the Haswell microarchitecture without TSX, operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores, 4.0 GB of system memory providing 2.0 GB per core, and 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not include a GPU.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, along with PassMark CPU and memory evaluations, rank in the bottom 10% of tested hardware. Memory bandwidth tests, including read-only and write operations on large blocks, also fall within the bottom 10%. Redis SET operations achieve 2.07 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is recorded at 1.89 GB/sec, both representing lower-tier performance.

Positioned as a budget-friendly option, the d2-4 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads that do not require sustained high-performance compute resources. Given the shared CPU allocation and baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps, this instance is best suited for lightweight applications, basic development environments, small-scale testing, or low-traffic static web hosting.
description: OVHcloud d2-4 is an entry-level virtual server from the Discovery family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 2 shared Intel vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, 4.0 GB of RAM, and 50 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results, including stress-ng CPU tests, PassMark scores, and memory bandwidth, consistently place this instance in the bottom 10% of performance tiers. It features a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps and includes one public IPv4 address. Given its shared resource model and lower-tier performance profile, the d2-4 is a highly cost-efficient option designed for lightweight workloads. It is best suited for basic development, testing, and low-traffic static web serving rather than resource-intensive database or production applications.
